title: Invoice variance after rate-limit failover — customer requests retroactive credit
creator: Ava Morales
description: Enterprise customer reported a 3x increase on their March invoice compared to expected usage. Support trace shows a spike coincident with a control-plane rate-limit event and automatic failover to a secondary routing path. Initial hypothesis: retry amplification combined with missing idempotency keys caused duplicate metering records to be counted against the customer. This ticket captures the investigation, corrective credits, and follow-up engineering work to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC: Customer opened support ticket reporting unexpected spike on March invoice.
2026-03-09 07:05 UTC: Support attached sample logs showing retry bursts and 503s from control plane during 01:30-02:00 UTC window.
2026-03-09 09:30 UTC: Pager duty alert routed to billing-engineering; initial triage assigned to Ravi.
2026-03-09 11:00 UTC: Replayed ingress logs and observed 3x repeated request IDs with sequential retry headers; metering ingestion accepted all as distinct.
2026-03-10 15:20 UTC: Confirmed failover from primary router to backup path when rate limiter hit 99th percentile for brief interval.
2026-03-11 09:00 UTC: Created reconciliation job to deduplicate meter lines by request footprint; ran against suspect time window.
2026-03-12 18:10 UTC: Legal/Finance approved provisional credit; customer notified of pending credit and investigation timeline.
2026-03-13 10:45 UTC: Deployments merged: proxy-level idempotency header honors and metering dedupe on ingestion (hotfixes in runtime-1.22 branch).
2026-03-13 16:00 UTC: Applied $12,480 credit to customer account; Finance journal REF-BILL-15643 created.
investigation_notes: Root cause: transient control-plane rate limiting produced 503s at the edge. Client SDK retried requests with exponential backoff but without stable idempotency token, and the internal proxy generated new request IDs on failover leading to separate metering records.
Metering ingestion accepted each unique request ID and did not correlate by client-provided fingerprint; ingestion dedupe window was 60s and keyed off request_id only.
We found 28,912 duplicated token-generation events for the affected customer during the 01:25-02:05 UTC window — accounting for the bulk of the spike.
A subset of retries were also re-sent by the customer's SDK (older SDK v1.3.2) with aggressive retry settings; reached out to customer success to recommend upgrade and backoff tuning.
No evidence of billing-side double-charging outside the failover window; outage limited to a single region and short duration.
steps_taken: Created immediate reconciliation script that groups meter lines by (customer_id, prompt_hash, approximate_timestamp) and collapses duplicates — lowered counted tokens for window by ~2.9M tokens.
Issued provisional credit equal to overage identified by reconciliation; Finance posted credit and notified customer billing contact.
Merged proxy change to honor X-Idempotency-Key and to surface original client token to metering layer (PR #2412).
Augmented metering ingestion to run a lightweight duplication check for repeated footprints within 5 minutes (PR #987).
Added alerting rule: sudden per-customer tokens/hour > 2x baseline AND simultaneous control-plane 5xxs triggers P0 investigation.
Filed SDK advisory for customers still on v1.x with suggested retry/backoff and idempotency guidance.
risk_and_tradeoffs: Short-term dedupe at ingestion reduces false positives but may hide genuine back-to-back calls from SDKs — tradeoff mitigated by conservative grouping heuristics and manual override for disputes.
Honoring client idempotency requires clients to set stable keys; we cannot enforce this for all customers. A supplemental server-side fingerprint is necessary as a backstop.
More aggressive retention of dedupe metadata increases storage and adds CPU cost to ingestion; we limited retention to 5 minutes in the hot path and do full reconciliation offline if needed.
resolution: Customer credited $12,480 (full amount of reconciled overage) on 2026-03-13. Hotfixes merged to proxy and metering ingestion; monitoring and alerting enhancements deployed to staging and scheduled for canary in runtime-1.22 on 2026-03-16. Customer (Solis HealthTech) accepted the credit and moved to 'monitoring' status with CSM.
follow_up_actions: 2026-03-16: Canary runtime-1.22 with proxy idempotency changes in us-west-2 for 48h (owner: Ravi).
2026-03-18: Ship metering ingestion dedupe to production if canary shows <0.1% false positives (owner: Mei Chen).
2026-03-23: Cross-team retrospective with Support, Finance, SDK, and SRE to codify billing dispute runbook and SLAs for provisional credits (owner: Ava).
Q2 2026: Add automatic reconciliation job that runs daily on all enterprise accounts flagged by alerting (owner: Billing TF).
notes: Recommendation: Add explicit guidance to enterprise onboarding for idempotency best practices and include SDK changes in enterprise upgrade emails.
We will provide customers an optional SDK hook to surface idempotency tokens automatically for critical request types.
Keep ticket open until canary completes and postmortem is published (target close: 2026-03-24).
